product.olivetti-m290sp.summary: 1991 M290 with a 20 MHz 286, VLSI TOPCAT chipset and integrated WD90C11 video.
product.olivetti-m290sp.history: The preserved BIOS identifies itself as "M290 SP" and belongs to the same firmware family later used by the M300 BA013 boards and the PCS 11/33. Its processor, chipset, video and memory match the BA-08 board of the M290-25 described in the Olivetti service guide, but no primary source found so far ties the name M290 SP to the BA-08. It is a different model from the original M290, which uses another BIOS, and from the 1986 M28 SP.
product.olivetti-m290sp.creation.model: M290 SP with a 20 MHz 286, 1 MB, integrated WD90C11 and one 3.5-inch 1.44 MB floppy drive
product.olivetti-m290sp.creation.storage: No hard disk: one 1.44 MB floppy drive
product.olivetti-m290sp.creation.note: The BIOS only supports six disk types. If you add the disk, select the type given in the option in Setup.
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.cpu: Intel 80286 at 20 MHz with a coprocessor socket. VLSI TOPCAT chipset: 82C320 (system controller) and 82C331 (bus controller). 8042 controller for the keyboard and PS/2 mouse.
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.memory: Banks 0 and 1 on the board: two soldered 256K × 18 devices, 512 KB each (1 MB). Banks 2 and 3 on the expansion card, each a pair of 1M × 9 (2 MB) or 4M × 9 (8 MB) SIMMs. 1 to 17 MB in total, 80 ns access.
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.video: Integrated VGA with a Western Digital WD90C11 (WD90C11A-LR in later revisions) and an ICS90C61 clock generator, with video memory sockets on the board. BluMach takes the character font from the firmware itself and sets the video chip's power-on state; that state has not been checked against a real board.
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.storag: National floppy controller with 1.2 MB (5.25") and 1.44 MB (3.5") drives, an IDE disk interface built from buffers and MSI logic, and serial and parallel ports in the 87C310. The BIOS 1.08 disk table has six types: 615/4/17, 980/5/17, 1014/9/18, 755/16/17, 762/8/39 and 873/13/36 (20 to 200 MB).
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.firmwa: One 128 KB image with Resident Diagnostics 1.08 and a ROM Setup in six languages. Copyright Olivetti 02/25/91. The BA-08 service guide lists revisions 1.04, 2.00 and 2.01 but not 1.08; according to the guide, 2.00 fixes random hangs, boot failures and A20 gate handling.
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.verifi: BIOS 1.08 is identified and verified by hash. In BluMach it completes the Resident Diagnostics (CPU, ROM, refresh, parity, interrupts, DMA, keyboard, clock, protected mode and CMOS), initialises VGA video, detects the IDE disk and boots MS-DOS from the hard disk.
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.limita: Experimental emulation. The TOPCAT is a partial functional model with the BA-08 bank layout; the timer timing and the board line the BIOS reads with keyboard-controller commands 8Ah/8Bh are set to what the firmware checks, not measured on a real board. Setup, the other memory sizes and more software remain to be validated.
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.identi: Link between the firmware name "M290 SP" and the M290-25/BA08 board: inferred from matching components, pending a primary source (service guide, board photo or EPROM label).
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.commer: The service guide presents the M290-25 with the BA-08 board and 1 MB on board, expandable to 17 MB with a memory card, three 16-bit slots on the bus card and 40, 85 or 120 MB hard disks.
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.setup: ROM Setup that opens by itself when the CMOS is invalid or the hardware changes. The extended Setup (EMS memory, shadowing, memory and bus speed, password) opens with Shift+Ctrl+Alt+Del.
product.olivetti-m290sp.technical.servic: Olivetti Personal Computer - Pocket Service Guide, chapter 32: M290-25 (BA-08).
